walkthroughs.body_html:
Internal Assessment: Historical Investigation — a core area of History.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Internal Assessment: Historical Investigation brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Internal Assessment: Historical Investigation.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which Bolshevik slogan summarised Lenin's April Theses?
options: Peace, Land, Bread
Workers of the world unite
Liberte, egalite, fraternite
Better dead than red

mcqs.q: What was the immediate cause of the February Revolution?
options: German invasion
Bread shortages in Petrograd
Lenin's return from Switzerland
Kerensky's offensive

mcqs.q: Did the Treaty of Versailles directly cause WWII?
options: Versailles caused WWII because it required Germany to invade Poland.
Versailles caused WWII directly because it was so harsh on Germany.
It contributed via German resentment and economic strain, but the 1930s Depression, Hitler's choices, and Allied appeasement were equally necessary — Versailles alone is not sufficient.
The Five Year Plans were Lenin's last great achievement.

mcqs.q: Why were 19th-century industrial cities so unhealthy?
options: Rapid population growth outpaced housing, water and sewage; lack of regulation produced overcrowded slums and cholera epidemics until reforms followed Chadwick's 1842 report.
Cities were unhealthy because Victorians did not care about hygiene.
The Five Year Plans were Lenin's last great achievement.
Cities were unhealthy because factory smoke poisoned the food.

mcqs.q: How successful were Stalin's Five Year Plans?
options: The Five Year Plans were Lenin's last great achievement.
The Five Year Plans turned the USSR into the most prosperous country in the world.
Heavy industry and steel output grew dramatically; consumer goods, quality and worker conditions lagged badly; statistics were inflated, but the USSR became an industrial power.
Versailles caused WWII because it required Germany to invade Poland.
